scope: Theorem 4.2 (Specialization detection) of the manuscript “Tame Hecke Eigensheaves with Several Marked Points” (preprints/Tame-Hecke-Eigensheaves-with-Several-Marked-Points-October-5-2026/Tame-Hecke-Eigensheaves-with-Several-Marked-Points.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 fb3f3a7a4115f5ec), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In this relative setup, let F ∈ Dlcc(Bη̄) be a Hecke eigen- complex with lisse eigenvalues on Lη̄ satisfying the lattice specialization condition of Proposition 2.2. If ΨF = 0, then on every smooth finite-type chart D → B the closure of the generic nonzero-stalk locus of F|Dη̄ does not meet Ds.
